title: Developer Toolkit Garden: Playbooks, Quickstarts, and Experiment Catalog
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: Build a curated ‘Toolkit Garden’ — a catalog of opinionated SDKs, minimal and opinionated quickstart templates, and playbooks for common vertical adoption patterns (chat assistant, embeddings search, summarization pipelines). The goal is to cut time-to-first-success (TTFS) for new developers and increase active SDK adoption across small- and mid-market customers.

Goals & success metrics (OKR-aligned):
- Reduce median TTFS from onboarding (sign-up to first successful API call + example app running) from ~18 minutes to <=6 minutes.
- Increase active SDK adoption (monthly active projects using SDKs) by 40% quarter-over-quarter.
- Ship 6 vetted quickstarts (Python, JavaScript/Node, Next.js, Go, Rust, and Serverless blueprint) with automated CI and sample billing that stays within free-tier.

Scope & deliverables:
- Experiment catalog: a living list of 12 short A/B experiments to evaluate onboarding flows (e.g., minimal CLI + example app vs guided web-runner). Each experiment includes hypothesis, metrics, tracking plan, required assets.
- Playbooks: 4 playbooks for common uses (chat assistant, semantic search, summarization, embeddings-based reranking) describing recommended SDKs, config profiles (batching/kv cache), quantization guidance, and cost/latency expectations.
- Quickstarts: opinionated templates with step-by-step README, test harness, CI, GitHub Codespaces/DevContainer, and a Deck with demo script for field engineers.
- Dashboard: a lightweight metric page in RED Dashboard (TTFS funnel, quickstart conversion, SDK installation errors, docs search signals).

Approach & trade-offs:
- Keep quickstarts opinionated to show best-case performance and recommended defaults (reduces cognitive load), while maintaining a minimal variant for advanced users. Trade-off: opinionated templates may hide advanced knobs — mitigate by explicit “advanced” section and link to full SDK docs.
- Prioritize Python and JavaScript flows for the first wave given usage signal; other languages will be simultaneous but phased.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1-3 (Discovery & prototypes): run 3 pilot experiments (Python minimal, Python opinionated, Next.js starter) with a small cohort of power users and 5 external beta partners.
- Week 4-6 (Refinement & docs): lock templates, write playbooks, instrument dashboard events.
- Week 7-9 (Public beta): publish quickstarts, ship Confluence playbooks, enable Codespaces templates, open PR templates.
- Week 10-12 (Measure & iterate): collect signals, run A/B of onboarding funnel, re-prioritize next 6 experiments.

Risks & mitigation: 
- Risk: Quickstarts that require paid capacity may deter users. Mitigation: provide local run scripts and guidance on free-tier models + sandbox tokens.
- Risk: Dependencies on runtime infra (ENG-84210 autoscaling changes) could block CI for heavy examples. Mitigation: coordinate with infra to create lightweight CI usage profile and fallback mocks.
